segments.text: HOUSTON: Oil prices settled 4 percent higher on Thursday on revived concerns about the ongoing war in the Middle East and growing supply disruptions due to a hurricane approaching the US Gulf Coast.

Brent crude futures closed up USD4.08, or 4.1 percent, at USD104.28, while US West Texas Intermediate crude rose 3.6 percent, or USD3.21, to USD91.49. At one point both contracts were up more than USD5 a barrel, with Brent touching its high

Iran’s Tasnim news agency reported that Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran is reviewing the US response to its proposal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, saying it would reply within days.
